headline: *#1* REASON
WALLS *FAIL*
beats.vo: Number one reason walls fail? Water. Here's how a good wall handles it.

headline: *WATER* PRESSURE
BREAKS WALLS
beats.vo: Rain soaks the soil behind the wall, and that *water pushes* on top of the soil load.

headline: DRAIN ROCK
+ *DRAIN PIPE*
beats.vo: A well-built block wall typically has about *twelve inches of drain rock* behind it and a *perforated pipe* at the base.

headline: THE PIPE NEEDS
AN *OUTLET*
beats.vo: And that pipe has to drain somewhere *approved*, never onto your *neighbour*.
Wall *bulging, leaning* or weeping water? Have an *engineer* take a look.

post.caption: The number one reason retaining walls fail in the Lower Mainland is water. A well-built block wall typically has about 12 inches of drain rock behind it and a perforated pipe at the base that drains to an approved outlet. Bulging, leaning or weeping? Have an engineer take a look.
post.alt: A slab walkway between two capped block retaining walls, an animated cross-section showing water pressure behind a wall and the drain rock and perforated pipe that relieve it, and a low angle on the block courses and caps of a finished retaining wall.
